sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast. My name is Amelia. I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Phnom Penh. Phnom Penh is the capital city of Cambodia.
It is a big, busy and interesting city. Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Are you ready? Let's begin. Part 1. Where is Phnom Penh? Phnom Penh is in Cambodia.
Cambodia is in Southeast Asia. It is between Thailand, Laos and Vietnam.
Phnom Penh is in the south of Cambodia. It is near the Mekong River. The city is very close to the
rivers. There are three rivers in Phnom Penh. The Mekong River, the Basak River and the Tonle Sap
River. Because of the rivers, Phnom Penh is a water city. It is very green and very alive.
The population of Phnom Penh is about 2 million people. That means many people live there. It is
the biggest city in Cambodia. It is also the most important city for business, culture and government.
Part 2. A short history of Phnom Penh. Phnom Penh has a long history. The name Phnom Penh means
Pen's Hill. Long ago there was a woman named Penh. She found statues of Buddha inside a tree.
She built a temple on a small hill for the statues. This place became the city. Today that hill is
called Wat Phnom. It is still very important. So the story of Phnom Penh begins with a woman
and a temple. Phnom Penh became the capital of Cambodia in the 15th century. Later the
capital moved to other places. In the 19th century Phnom Penh became the capital again.
At that time the French came to Cambodia. The French made new buildings, streets and markets.
That is why Phnom Penh has many French style buildings. They are very beautiful. In the 1970s
Cambodia had a very sad time. It was the Khmer Rouge period. Many people died. Phnom Penh was
almost empty. After that time people came back. Now Phnom Penh is growing and changing.
It is a city of history, sadness and also new hope. Part 3. The people. The people of Phnom Penh
are Cambodian. They speak the Khmer language. Many people also speak some English. People are
friendly and welcoming. They smile a lot. They like to help visitors. Most people in Phnom Penh
are Buddhist. You can see many monks in the city. They wear orange clothes. They walk on the streets.
They go to temples. Buddhism is very important in daily life. Families in Phnom Penh are big.
They like to spend time together. They eat together. They celebrate together.
Respect for parents and elders is very important. Part 4. Culture in Phnom Penh
Phnom Penh is the cultural heart of Cambodia. There are many temples, museums and art places.
The royal palace is very famous. It is where the king of Cambodia lives. The palace is beautiful
and golden. Near the palace there is the silver pagoda. It has a floor with silver tiles.
Another important place is the National Museum. It has many old statues, art and history.
It shows the Khmer culture. Visitors can learn about Cambodia here. Phnom Penh also has traditional
dance and music. The most famous dance is the Absara dance. Dancers wear beautiful clothes.
They move slowly and with their hands. It looks like a story in movement.
Part 5. Food in Phnom Penh
Food in Phnom Penh is delicious. People eat rice every day. Rice is the main food.
Fish is also very important. The Mekong River gives a lot of fish. A famous dish is a mock.
It is fish with coconut milk and spices. It is cooked in a banana leaf. It tastes very good.
Another food is namban chalk. It is rice noodles with green curry. People eat it for breakfast.
Street food is popular in Phnom Penh. You can find fried noodles, grilled meat, fresh fruit and
sweet cakes. On the street food is cheap and tasty. People also drink sugar cane juice,
ice coffee and tea. The weather is hot so cold drinks are popular.
Part 6. Famous Places in Phnom Penh
Let's talk about some famous places in Phnom Penh.
It is the place where the city started. Many people go there to pray.
Royal Palace. This is where the king lives. It is big, golden and very beautiful.
Silver Pagoda. This is inside the Royal Palace area. The floor has thousands of silver tiles.
National Museum. This is a museum with Khmer art and history.
Independence Monument. This is a tall monument in the city. It celebrates Cambodia's independence
from France. Central Market. This is a very big market. The building is round. People sell clothes,
jewelry, food and many things. Russian Market. This is another market. You can buy souvenirs,
art and clothes here. Tool slang genocide museum. This is a sad place. It was a school
then a prison during the Khmer Rouge time. Many people died here. Now it is a museum to
remember the past. Killing Fields. This is outside Phnom Penh. It is another sad place.
It shows the history of the Khmer Rouge. It is important to learn about it. Phnom Penh
has both happy and sad places. Together they tell the story of the city.
Part 7. Daily Life in Phnom Penh. Life in Phnom Penh is busy. The streets are full of cars,
buses and motorbikes. Motorbikes are the most common. Many people use tuck tucks too.
A tuck tuck is a small taxi with three wheels. Visitors often use tuck tucks. The weather is hot
and wet. There are two seasons. Dry season and rainy season. The dry season is from November to
April. The rainy season is from May to October. In the rainy season, it rains a lot. The streets
can be full of water. People in Phnom Penh like to go to markets. Markets are the center of life.
You can buy food, clothes and daily things there. Markets are colorful, noisy and fun.
Children go to school in the morning or afternoon. Many schools are in the city.
Students wear uniforms. In the evening, people go outside. They eat at street stalls. They sit
by the river. They talk with friends. The city feels alive. Part 8. Fun and Relaxation.
Phnom Penh is also a place for fun. By the river side, there are many restaurants and cafes.
People like to eat and watch the river. There are also shopping malls.
Young people go there to shop and watch movies. At night, the city has lights, music and shows.
Some people go to clubs. Others enjoy live music or dance. Many visitors like to take a boat on the
Mekong River. At sunset, the view is beautiful. The sky is red and orange. The river is calm.
It is very peaceful. Part 9. Nature around Phnom Penh. Phnom Penh is a city, but nature is close.
The rivers give life to the city. There are parks and green spaces. People like to walk and relax
in the parks. Outside the city, there are rice fields and villages. People farm and fish.
It is simple and quiet. This shows another side of Cambodia. Part 10. Why visit Phnom Penh?
Phnom Penh is a city of contrasts. It has old temples and new buildings. It has sad history
and new hope. It has busy markets and quiet temples. It has traditional food and modern cafes.
Visitors can learn about Cambodia's past and present. They can see culture, taste food and
meet kind people. Phnom Penh is not just a capital. It is the heart of Cambodia. Outro.
That is all for today. Now you know many things about Phnom Penh. It is a big busy and interesting
city. It has history, culture, food and kind people. I hope you learned something new today.
